briefings.title: AIPCon 9 March 2026 | Livestream
briefings.tldr: Palantir has shifted from traditional software delivery to an "industrial operating system" model that prioritizes "decision advantage," reducing complex operational cycles from weeks to seconds across defense, energy, and commercial sectors.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Palantir has shifted from traditional software delivery to an "industrial operating system" model that prioritizes "decision advantage," reducing complex operational cycles from weeks to seconds across defense, energy, and commercial sectors. The company’s core value proposition is the rapid deployment of AI-driven ontologies that empower "substantive operators" to outperform competitors and adversaries through superior execution and real-time visibility.

## Defense and National Security: Achieving "Decision Advantage"
*   **Project Maven & Global Targeting:** Palantir’s Maverick/Maven Smart System has evolved from simple computer vision to a comprehensive "battle space awareness" tool.
    *   **Decision-Centric Workflows:** Cameron Stanley (CDIO, Dept. of War) emphasized shifting focus from "AI detections" to "workflow acceleration," collapsing kill chains that previously took hours into minutes via a single fused visualization and action layer.
    *   **Resource Efficiency:** Automation allows 20 intelligence officers to perform targeting tasks that previously required 2,000 personnel.
*   **ShipOS and Naval Readiness:** Vice Admiral Seiko Okano (US Navy) introduced ShipOS, an AI-enabled operating system for the naval shipbuilding industrial base.
    *   **Operational Impact:** Targeted at submarine construction (specifically HALEU fuel and J85 engines), the system identifies material risks and schedule gaps before they manifest.
    *   **Efficiency Gains:** BOM (Bill of Materials) approval times were reduced from **200 hours to 15 seconds**. Contract review cycles and project backlogs saw similar drastic reductions.
*   **Pro-Warfighter Stance:** CEO Dr. Alex Karp reiterated Palantir's non-monolithic but staunchly pro-military culture, stating that the company’s priority is providing an "unfair advantage" to U.S. and allied forces.

## Industrial Scaling and Energy Sovereignty
*   **Nuclear Fuel Production (Centrus Energy):** Patrick Brown (SVP, Centrus) announced a partnership to restore U.S. uranium enrichment capacity.
    *   **Expansion Scale:** Moving from 16 experimental centrifuges to a phase-one goal of **11,520 machines**.
    *   **Real-time Oversight:** AIP replaced paper-based processes and an 8-week data lag with a "Centrifuge Mission Control," providing instant visibility into supplier risks and crew constraints.
*   **Aerospace Sustainment (GE Aerospace):** Jess Salzbrun (CIO, GE Aerospace) detailed the use of Palantir to manage the J85 engine, which powers the T-38 trainer fleet.
    *   **Predictive Maintenance:** The system monitors **6,000 individual piece parts**, predicting constraints 12 months in advance to ensure fleet readiness.
*   **Stratospheric Intelligence (World View):** Ryan Hartman (CEO, World View) highlighted the "AI Flight Director" built on Palantir Maverick.
    *   **Time Compression:** Reduced mission planning for stratospheric balloons from **two weeks to a few hours**, enabling "swarming" capabilities for persistent ISR (Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance).

## Enterprise Transformation and Cloud Migration
*   **The SAP/Accenture Alliance:** Sebastian Steinhaeuser (COO, SAP) and Tracy Venable (Accenture) announced a massive expansion of their partnership with Palantir to solve the "Mordor-like" complexity of ERP migrations.
    *   **Performance Metrics:** Joint engagements show **99% validation accuracy** within two weeks and a **70% reduction in timeline and cost** for migrations.
    *   **Rapid Assessment:** Customers receive a validated migration execution plan in as little as 10 days.
*   **Healthcare Accreditation (The Joint Commission):** William Walders (CDIO) detailed "Reforge," a digital control plane that integrated **400 disparate applications**.
    *   **Public Impact:** The system created public clarity on healthcare standards and reduced the burden of 5-day on-site hospital inspections through real-time "accreditation scores."
*   **Mortgage Efficiency (Freedom Mortgage):** Michael Middleman (Vice Chairman) is using AIP to address home ownership affordability by automating regulatory audits and document extraction, turning "months of IT projects into minutes or hours."

## The New Engagement Model: Extreme Pacing
*   **Accelerated Deployment:** Ryan Taylor (Palantir) noted a "step change" in deployment speed, with teams now building production-ready applications in **24 to 48 hours** rather than months.
    *   **Disruption Management:** A global logistics provider built a "disruption manager" in a single afternoon to reroute cargo during cartel violence in Mexico.
    *   **Fleet Optimization:** An automotive customer built four state-of-the-art predictive models and an automated routing engine for tens of thousands of assets in just four days.
*   **The 30-Day Social Contract:** Taylor proposed a new aggressive partnership model:
    *   **Day 1:** Build initial solutions.
    *   **Week 1:** Expand to upstream/downstream workflows.
    *   **Day 30:** Finalize a 12-month transformation plan to integrate AI across the entire business.

## Notable Quotes
> "If you're expecting us to not support warfighters when they're in battle... you got the wrong company... we are very, very proud to have our role in making sure the American men and women come home safe."
— **Dr. Alex Karp**, CEO, Palantir

> "The faster path to a stronger fleet runs directly through a smarter, more agile industrial base. ShipOS is how we turn that decision into results... capability to the fleet delivered at speed."
— **Vice Admiral Seiko Okano**, US Navy

> "You can now build Iron Man suits around those people so that they can do a thousand X what they could do before and set the standard for what is unique about your organization."
— **Ryan Taylor**, Palantir

> "Every single tool that I get from my vendors, Palantir especially, updates with time. It’s the first time in my career that I have a system that gets better day after day."
— **Cameron Stanley**, CDIO, U.S. Department of War

briefings.title: BlackRock CEO on if US-Iran conflict could derail economy as gas prices surge
briefings.tldr: BlackRock CEO Larry Fink views current geopolitical volatility as a long-term "buying opportunity," asserting that the U.S. economy is entering a transformational era driven by a $10 trillion infrastructure need and AI-led productivity, which necessitates a massive reinvestment in skilled domestic labor.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
BlackRock CEO Larry Fink views current geopolitical volatility as a long-term "buying opportunity," asserting that the U.S. economy is entering a transformational era driven by a $10 trillion infrastructure need and AI-led productivity, which necessitates a massive reinvestment in skilled domestic labor.

## Geopolitics and Energy Market Outlook
* **Market Volatility:** Larry Fink characterizes the current uncertainty surrounding Iran as short-term noise. He advises investors to ignore immediate volatility in favor of long-dated trends, suggesting that current market dips are a "buy" opportunity.
* **Oil Price Projections:** While prices have spiked recently, Fink predicts a potential reversion to lower prices. 
    * If the conflict leads to a "neutralized" Iran that returns to the global market, oil could drop below $50 per barrel.
* **Economic Resilience:** Fink notes that despite tariffs and geopolitical tension, the market has adjusted rapidly. He credits AI-driven deflationary trends for offsetting the inflationary pressures typically caused by import costs.

## The $10 Trillion AI Infrastructure Gap
* **Transformational Technology:** Fink compares the impact of AI to the introduction of the steam engine in the 19th century, predicting it will reshape the global economy and radically increase productivity.
* **Investment Requirements:** BlackRock estimates a need for **$10 trillion in U.S. infrastructure investment** over the next eight years to support the AI transition.
    * **Grid and Data Centers:** Massive capital is required to build out the electrical grid, data centers, and ensure energy resilience.
    * **Job Creation:** While AI may eliminate some roles, it is expected to create high-paying jobs ($100k–$150k) in construction and technical trades.

## The Skilled Labor Crisis and "Future Builders"
* **Demographic Deficit:** The U.S. workforce faces a "clear and present" crisis in skilled trades; currently, for every five workers who retire, only two enter the field.
* **Future Builders Initiative:** The BlackRock Foundation is launching a $100 million, five-year program to address this gap.
    * **Goal:** To train 50,000 Americans in essential trades like plumbing and electrical work.
    * **Strategic Necessity:** Fink argues that if the U.S. does not solve its labor shortage and win the infrastructure race, China will dominate the global technological landscape.

## Strategic Competition and the Shift to Pragmatism
* **US-China Relations:** Fink views China as both a critical trade partner (specifically for U.S. agriculture) and a primary adversary. 
    * **Tech Dispersion:** He argues the stakes of the rivalry are "broader than winning" at home; the goal is ensuring U.S. allies use American technology rather than Chinese alternatives.
* **Fiduciary Pragmatism:** Addressing criticisms of "woke" investing and ESG, Fink states the "pendulum" swung too far five years ago and is now returning to a more pragmatic center.
    * **Energy Mix:** He emphasizes a "fiduciary-first" approach, investing in both hydrocarbons (e.g., carbon capture with Occidental Petroleum) and renewables (solar and nuclear) based on client demand.
    * **Global Trends:** He notes that even China is aggressively pursuing a "mixed" energy strategy, leading the world in both nuclear/solar build-out and gas/oil imports.

> "We estimate there's going to be a need for 10 trillion dollars of investing in the United States alone over the course of the next eight years... We don't have enough skilled workers to meet the needs of these jobs. We're not ready for it and we have to win. If we don't win this, China's going to win." — **Larry Fink**

> "I don't pay much attention to this short-term volatility, but I focus more on these longer-term trends... I've been getting so many texts: 'What should I do?' And I said, 'Buy more here,' because this is a good long-term opportunity." — **Larry Fink**

> "Do I believe the pendulum five years ago was too far [on ESG]? Yes. I personally am more pragmatic, too... today, because of AI and the overwhelming need for power and electricity, it can't just be one way right now. It can't just be hydrocarbons." — **Larry Fink**

briefings.title: Blackrock Infrastructure Summit: Future Builders | Semafor Media Partner
briefings.tldr: BlackRock is launching a $100 million "Future Builders" initiative to address a critical skilled labor shortage that threatens U.S. infrastructure and global competitiveness.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
BlackRock is launching a $100 million "Future Builders" initiative to address a critical skilled labor shortage that threatens U.S. infrastructure and global competitiveness. As AI disrupts white-collar professions, leaders emphasize a cultural and economic shift toward the trades, where high demand and massive infrastructure investments are creating lucrative, non-degree career paths.

## The Skilled Labor Crisis and the "Future Builders" Initiative
* **Closing the Gap:** The BlackRock Foundation has committed $100 million to a national philanthropic initiative focused on connecting workers to skilled trades training.
    * **Market Demand:** According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, hundreds of thousands of net new skilled trade jobs are required to meet current infrastructure demand.
    * **The "Work" Gap:** There are currently 7.6 million open positions in the U.S., while 6.9 million prime-working-age men are affirmatively not looking for work.
* **The "Shop Class" Consequence:** Mike Rowe attributed the current crisis to the removal of vocational training from high schools in the 1970s.
    * **Cultural Stigma:** The trades were framed as a "vocational consolation prize," leading to a generation that views aspirational careers as exclusively degree-based.
    * **Retirement Wave:** For every five skilled tradespeople who leave the workforce, only two enter, creating an existential threat to the maritime, energy, and construction industries.

## AI Disruption and the Recalibration of Education
* **The Value of Degrees:** While Larry Fink acknowledged the social value of college, he noted that tuition has outpaced inflation for 30 years, undermining the value proposition for many students.
    * **AI Impact:** AI is expected to disrupt white-collar "whiteboard" jobs faster than manual trades, potentially leading to high unemployment among college graduates even in a growing economy.
    * **High-Earning Trades:** Mike Rowe cited data center electricians under age 30 earning $240,000 to $280,000 annually without college debt, noting they are frequently "poached" by competitors due to scarcity.
* **Corporate Shifts:** BlackRock is seeing revenue growth outpace headcount growth as technology allows the firm to "do more with fewer people," a trend expected to accelerate across the corporate sector.

## Infrastructure as a National Security Imperative
* **Global Competition:** Fink warned that if the U.S. does not develop abundant, affordable power and modern infrastructure, "China wins."
    * **Energy Strategy:** China is currently building 100 gigawatts of nuclear power and miles of solar fields; the U.S. must accelerate solar, battery storage, and hydrocarbon development to compete.
    * **Capital Requirements:** An estimated $10 trillion of investable money is needed over the next eight years to rebuild American infrastructure.
* **Onshoring Manufacturing:** Fink advocated for a "51% ownership" model—similar to China’s requirements—to bring Korean or Chinese battery and solar manufacturers to the U.S. to create local jobs.

## Financial Literacy and the Wealth Gap
* **Broadening Participation:** Currently, 40% of Americans have no capacity to invest in the financial markets. Fink argues that the wealth gap is driven by capital appreciating faster than salaries.
    * **Retirement Solutions:** BlackRock advocates for "childhood accounts" (starting with $1,000) to allow every citizen to benefit from the "technological boom" and long-term market growth.
* **The "Jumpstart Bill":** Mike Rowe highlighted proposed legislation (the Jumpstart Act) that would allow 529 plans to be used for "tools of the trade," such as trucks and equipment, rather than just tuition.
* **Economic Outlook:** Fink expressed minimal concern regarding long-term inflation, suggesting that if wage growth is coupled with technology-driven productivity, the net result is a "good outcome" for the economy.

## Notable Quotes

> "Nothing in the history of Western civilization has gotten more expensive more quickly than a four-year degree. It’s not to say it’s not valuable, but... we encouraged kids to borrow whatever it took to take that path... and told them if you don't, you're screwed."
— **Mike Rowe**, Founder, mikeroweWORKS Foundation

> "If we don't rebuild America's infrastructure, if we do not have an America that has abundant power that is affordable, which is the foundation for AI—if we don't have that, China wins."
— **Larry Fink**, Chairman and CEO, BlackRock

> "What the country needs are more philosophers who can run an even bead [weld] and appreciate the magnificence of something built, and more welders who can have a conversation about the Stoics... The color of collars is over."
— **Mike Rowe**, Founder, mikeroweWORKS Foundation

> "I am more bullish on the United States than any other country... but we need more and more Americans investing in this growth or having a piece of the American growth. We don't talk about that enough."
— **Larry Fink**, Chairman and CEO, BlackRock

briefings.title: 🔴 Dr. Alex Karp LIVE on TBPN
briefings.tldr: Palantir and industry analysts characterize the current AI era as a "Fourth Industrial Revolution" that is rapidly transforming commercial sectors, accelerating software deployment to near-zero latency, and necessitating a radical shift in labor skills to survive significant white-collar job displacement.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Palantir and industry analysts characterize the current AI era as a "Fourth Industrial Revolution" that is rapidly transforming commercial sectors, accelerating software deployment to near-zero latency, and necessitating a radical shift in labor skills to survive significant white-collar job displacement.

## The AI Market Outlook and "Golden Child" Status
* **Palantir’s Market Position:** Dan Ives (Managing Director, Wedbush Securities) identifies Palantir as the "golden child" and "poster child" of the AI revolution.
    * **Financial Growth:** The commercial business is the primary driver of Wall Street interest; Ives predicts the combined government and commercial sectors could lead Palantir to a trillion-dollar valuation within two to three years.
    * **The "Ghost Trade":** Ives describes the current software market as a "ghost trade" where legacy companies are struggling to compete against new AI-native stacks and install bases.
* **Broader Tech Predictions:** 
    * **NVIDIA:** Labeled the "godfather of AI," NVIDIA is expected to reach a $6 trillion market cap by 2027 as they move toward owning end-to-end platforms.
    * **Tesla:** Positioned as a premier "physical AI" play; autonomous driving capabilities are estimated to be worth $1 trillion alone.
* **Investment Strategy:** Despite geopolitical tensions, Ives argues that selling is historically the wrong move during "white-knuckle moments." He maintains that tech stocks will likely hit new all-time highs this year.

## Transforming Infrastructure and Vertical Markets
* **Defense and Drones:** Eric Brock (Chairman & CEO, Ondas) highlights the shift from drones as commodities to drones as autonomous systems.
    * **Counter-Drone Infrastructure:** Protecting global locations from drone threats is viewed as a decade-long infrastructure build-out rather than a short-term military trend.
    * **Integration:** Ondas is focused on a "system of systems" approach, integrating air and ground robots via platforms like Palantir.
* **Western Sports Analytics:** Casey Lane (Teton Ridge) explains the application of Palantir’s technology to rodeo and bull riding.
    * **"Moneyball" for Rodeo:** Teton Ridge is building a video analytics platform to track animals and riders, creating predictive models for performance and scoring.
    * **Viewer Engagement:** Using data to explain complex scoring to fans, similar to "Next Gen Stats" in the NFL.

## The Evolution of Software Engineering (FDE Model)
* **Accelerated Deployment:** Ted Mabrey (Palantir, 16-year veteran) reports that the pace of software deployment is "accelerating to zero." Applications that used to take years to develop are now reaching MVP (Minimum Viable Product) status in days or weeks.
* **The "Iron Man Suit" for Operations:** The role of the Forward-Deployed Engineer (FDE) has shifted from standardizing management tools to empowering "the guy at the edge" (e.g., a plant manager).
    * **Operational Experts:** Software is now designed to act as an "Iron Man suit" for subject matter experts, allowing them to dictate how the system runs based on real-world tribal knowledge.
* **Infrastructure Strategy:** Palantir’s core philosophy is building adaptive infrastructure that presumes models will constantly improve, rather than building rigid, legacy-limited systems.

## Geopolitics, Job Loss, and Civil Liberties
* **White-Collar Displacement:** Dr. Alex Karp (CEO, Palantir) issues a stark warning regarding AI-driven job loss, particularly for "Lawyer 14506"—the average, non-specialized white-collar worker.
    * **The "Dyslexic" Advantage:** Karp argues that "normal-shaped skills" are becoming less valuable. He suggests that "neuro-divergent" individuals and those with "artistry" who look at things from unique directions will thrive in the new economy.
* **National Security and Sovereignty:**
    * **US vs. China:** The world is viewed as a "have/have-not" binary between American and Chinese AI capabilities. Karp argues that America must win on the battlefield to protect domestic order.
    * **Nationalization Risks:** Karp predicts a future political movement toward nationalizing AI technology as displacement causes social unrest.
* **Privacy and Rights:** Karp positions himself as a defender of Fourth Amendment (privacy) rights at the executive table, arguing that while AI must be lethal on the battlefield, its domestic use must be strictly litigated to prevent government overreach.

> "I Odin this is come down... I’m going to make the world just right for a dyslexic. It’s really an inversion. Everybody with the normal shaped skills are dyslexics because the thing they can do that used to be valuable is not so valuable." — **Dr. Alex Karp**

> "Palantir continues to be one where I think investors continue to underestimate just how big they’re going to be in this AI revolution... could really ultimately be a trillion-dollar company in the next two to three years." — **Dan Ives**

> "We want to spend virtually no time explaining why it works and just showing you how it works and then let’s talk about how to make it work ten times better for you." — **Ted Mabrey**

> "The private equity model is saying I’m going to take this new form of cognition and try and replace old forms of cognition and do the exact same thing I’m doing before with slightly fewer heads... That is a dramatic underuse of the technology." — **Dr. Alex Karp**

briefings.title: Elon Musk: Optimus 3 Is Coming, Recursive Self-Improvement Is Already Here, and the Singularity #239
briefings.tldr: Elon Musk predicts a "hard takeoff" for AI with full recursive self-improvement by 2025, leading to a 10x expansion of the global economy within a decade and an eventual post-scarcity era of "Universal High Income."
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Elon Musk predicts a "hard takeoff" for AI with full recursive self-improvement by 2025, leading to a 10x expansion of the global economy within a decade and an eventual post-scarcity era of "Universal High Income."

## AI Evolution and Recursive Self-Improvement
* **Human-Out-of-the-Loop:** Musk states that we are already in a "hard takeoff" phase where successive AI models are built by their predecessors. Full automation of model building—recursive self-improvement without humans in the loop—is expected by the end of 2024 or 2025.
* **Grok Performance Benchmarks:**
    * **Prediction:** Musk claims Grok 1.5 is currently the best model for predictive tasks.
    * **Coding:** While currently trailing competitors, Musk expects Grok to "catch up and exceed" rivals in coding capabilities by mid-2024.
* **The Intelligence Explosion:** Future AI intelligence is expected to exceed human intelligence by orders of magnitude that are currently impossible to comprehend. Musk envisions a future where intelligence harnesses a million times more energy than Earth's current total electricity usage.

## The Robotics Revolution: Optimus Timeline
* **Production Schedule:** The "Optimus 2" humanoid robot is in final development. Production is slated to begin Summer 2024 with a slow initial ramp, reaching high-volume production in 2025.
* **Annual Design Cycles:** Musk intends to release a new, improved robot design every year, with "Optimus 3" already planned for a 2025 design phase.
* **Manufacturing Scale:**
    * Tesla is building roughly 10 million square feet of factory space specifically for Optimus production.
    * While Tesla employs ~150,000 people, Musk anticipates that automation will make the "output per human" extraordinarily high, though he does not foresee immediate layoffs.

## Macroeconomic Projections and "Universal High Income"
* **10x Economic Growth:** Barring World War III, Musk predicts the global economy will be more than 10 times its current size within 10 years.
* **Universal High Income (UHI):** Musk suggests the world will move beyond Universal Basic Income (UBI) to "Universal High Income." 
    * **Deflationary Abundance:** Because AI and robots will produce goods and services at a rate far exceeding the money supply, massive deflation will occur, making products essentially "saturated" and widely available.
* **The Irrelevance of Money:** Musk envisions a post-capitalist future similar to Ian Banks' *Culture* series, where traditional currency becomes irrelevant and the only meaningful metrics are "wattage and tonnage" (power and mass).

## Space Exploration and the Singularity
* **Ten-Year Space Milestones:** Musk expects a permanent base on the Moon, the implementation of "mass drivers" (electromagnetic catapults) on the lunar surface, and a human presence on Mars within the next decade.
* **Solar System Intelligence:** Musk notes that Earth only intercepts half a billionth of the Sun’s energy. He predicts the majority of future intelligence will eventually exist off-planet to harness the Sun's full energy output.
* **Solving Human Suffering:** Musk believes super-intelligence will solve "everything you can possibly think of," specifically citing the elimination of back pain and the extension of human healthspan as primary benefits.

## Notable Quotes

> "Humans are gradually getting less and less in the loop on recursive self-improvement. Every successive model is built by the one before it... It may be there end of this year, but not later than next year." — **Elon Musk**

> "I'd say the economy is ten times its current size in ten years. Greater than. In the absence of World War III, if current trends continue, I would say the economy 10x's in ten years." — **Elon Musk**

> "AI and robotics is also the only way we're going to solve our budget deficit frankly, and not just go bankrupt as a country." — **Elon Musk**

> "The challenge will be even vaguely appreciating that level of intelligence. But it's safe to say it will solve everything you can possibly think of. Longevity being certainly one of them." — **Elon Musk**

briefings.title: Louis Gave: $120 Oil Breaks Everything — And Nobody Is Ready

people.name: Julia La Roche
people.role: Host, The Julia La Roche Show

briefings.tldr: Louis Gave argues that the global economy has entered a structurally inflationary regime where energy prices serve as the primary risk and essential equity hedge, rendering the traditional 60/40 portfolio obsolete.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Louis Gave argues that the global economy has entered a structurally inflationary regime where energy prices serve as the primary risk and essential equity hedge, rendering the traditional 60/40 portfolio obsolete. While the U.S. remains energy-resilient, Gave warns that sustained oil prices above $120/barrel will "break" global allies and highlights a massive investment opportunity in the "stupidly undervalued" Chinese Renminbi.

## The Three Prices Driving the Macro Framework
*   **The Critical Pillars:** Gave’s investment process is dictated by three primary prices: the **U.S. Dollar**, the **10-year U.S. Treasury yield**, and the **price of energy**. Getting the direction of these three right accounts for 80-90% of investment success.
*   **The Bonds-War Correlation:** Following the insight of Luke Gromen, Gave notes that "bonds are the second casualty of war." In a conflict scenario, bonds suffer because wars are inherently inflationary events.
*   **The Binary Iran Outcome:**
    *   **Scenario A (Prolonged Conflict):** Continued instability in the Straits of Hormuz leads to supply chain dislocations and an inflationary hit to the economy, which is disastrous for bonds.
    *   **Scenario B (Regime Change):** While a "Berlin Wall" moment in Iran would be long-term bullish, the massive demand for capital to rebuild the Middle East would likely drive real interest rates significantly higher, as seen during German reunification.

## Energy as the New Portfolio Hedge
*   **The Death of 60/40:** The traditional 60% equity/40% bond portfolio thrived in a deflationary era. In today’s structurally inflationary world, bonds no longer provide protection against geopolitical or supply-side shocks.
*   **The 60/20/20 Rule:** Gave recommends a new allocation: **60% Equities, 20% Precious Metals, and 20% Energy**.
    *   **Energy as Protection:** In an inflationary bust, energy is the only asset that hedges against the primary risk—a spike in energy costs that collapses growth.
*   **Oil Price Thresholds:** 
    *   **$120/barrel:** This is the "break point" where high costs begin to crush U.S. consumption and global growth.
    *   **Market Mispricing:** Current futures markets suggest the oil spike is temporary. Gave disagrees, fearing the upside risk is more consequential and lasting than the market currently prices in.

## Geopolitical Resilience: U.S. vs. Global Allies
*   **U.S. Self-Sufficiency:** Because the U.S. is energy self-sufficient, $100+ oil is essentially a "right pocket, left pocket" transfer within the domestic economy (from consumers to energy-producing states like Texas and North Dakota).
*   **The Fragility of Allies:** High oil prices are catastrophic for Europe and East Asia. 
    *   **Supply Dependency:** 90% of oil flowing through the Straits of Hormuz goes East to China, India, Japan, and Korea.
    *   **Natural Gas Crisis:** Taiwan has only roughly 10 days of natural gas reserves; any prolonged blockage of trade routes forces a shift back to coal and creates a massive "global growth shock."
*   **The Weaponization of Treasuries:** Since the seizure of Russian assets, central banks (China, Saudi Arabia, etc.) no longer view U.S. Treasuries as risk-free. This has fueled a parabolic run in gold as central banks diversify away from Western sovereign debt.

## The China Misconception and the Trade War "Win"
*   **The Trade War Outcome:** Gave asserts that China won the trade war, albeit at a high domestic cost.
    *   **Evidence:** China’s trade surplus has grown from $20 billion/month to $100 billion/month since the conflict began.
    *   **De-Westernization:** China successfully spent the last eight years de-Westernizing its supply chains, making it resilient to U.S. embargoes in critical sectors like semiconductors and AI.
*   **The "Hunger Games" of Capitalism:** Contrary to the "central planning" narrative, China's growth is driven by hyper-competition. For example, local government incentives created 100 electric car producers, of which only a few survive, resulting in world-class EVs priced under $10,000.
*   **The Renminbi Opportunity:** 
    *   **Undervaluation:** The Renminbi is the most undervalued asset in the world due to massive productivity gains and domestic deflation that have not been priced into the currency.
    *   **Investment Case:** With zero inflation, China has the most room for fiscal and monetary easing compared to the West.

> "Economic activity is energy transformed... The lower an energy price, the easier it is for entrepreneurs to transform energy into corporate profits and into economic growth." — Louis Gave

> "If truth is the first casualty of war, bonds are usually a close second." — Louis Gave (quoting Luke Gromen)

> "The Renminbi is just stupidly stupidly undervalued... You can't understand how cheap the Renminbi is until you go visit China yourself... This is the obvious trade of the coming years." — Louis Gave

briefings.title: MacroVoices #523 Jim Bianco: Energy, FED & Economy in the wake of Iran conflict
briefings.tldr: The Iran conflict and resulting energy price spikes likely push U.S. inflation above 3%, effectively taking Fed rate cuts off the table to avoid spooking bond markets.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The Iran conflict and resulting energy price spikes likely push U.S. inflation above 3%, effectively taking Fed rate cuts off the table to avoid spooking bond markets. Concurrently, a structural decline in U.S. population growth means the economy no longer requires high monthly job creation to remain in balance, complicating traditional recession signals.

## Energy Markets and Inflationary Risks
* **Strait of Hormuz Blockage:** Jim Bianco characterizes crude oil as the world’s "circulatory system," currently facing a significant blockage.
    * While infrastructure remains intact, the risk of a "broken system" increases the longer the kinetic conflict persists.
    * **Market Signal:** WTI crude futures hit a record 25% backwardation on March 8th, signaling that the market currently expects the disruption to be short-term (2–3 months).
* **Impact on CPI:** Gasoline prices rose 18% ($0.55) in the first nine days of the conflict.
    * This spike is projected to produce a March CPI report of 0.6% or 0.7%, pushing year-over-year inflation above 3%.
    * High energy costs act as a "fire" that reinforces broader inflationary trends, making it difficult for the Fed to intervene.

## The Federal Reserve and Monetary Policy
* **Rate Cut Constraint:** Bianco argues the Fed "cannot" (or should not) cut rates with inflation above 3%. 
    * Doing so would signal to bond traders that the Fed is ignoring real returns, potentially causing a sell-off in the 10-year note and inadvertently tightening financial conditions.
* **Leadership Transition:** Kevin Warsh is expected to succeed Jerome Powell, with his first meeting as Chair likely in June.
    * **Fed Independence:** Bianco notes a shift toward more independent voting and frequent dissents within the Fed. 
    * Watching the Fed is now a "vote tallying" exercise rather than parsing the Chairman's words; currently, 10 of 12 voters lean hawkish, making a majority for rate cuts unlikely.

## Structural Shifts in the U.S. Labor Market
* **New Labor Equilibrium:** The U.S. economy no longer needs to create 150,000 jobs per month to stay healthy. 
    * **Population Growth:** Due to slowing immigration and low fertility rates, the working-age population (16–64) is stagnant.
    * The "breakeven" number for job growth is now likely between 0 and 50,000 per month.
* **Interpreting Weak Data:** February's loss of 90,000 jobs did not tank the market because the unemployment rate remained stable (4.4%). 
    * This suggests the labor market is in balance despite low headline numbers, making aggressive Fed stimulus unnecessary and potentially over-stimulative.

## Digital Assets and Stablecoin Statecraft
* **Stablecoin Hegemony:** The U.S. dollar is maintaining reserve status via digital "dollarization" in struggling economies like Venezuela, Iran, and Afghanistan.
    * Citizens in these regions use Tether and other stablecoins on smartphones to bypass failed local banking systems and government regulations.
* **The "Genius Act" and Substitution:** While some argue stablecoins will create massive new demand for Treasuries, Bianco views this as a "substitution effect."
    * Capital moving into stablecoins typically exits the traditional banking system, which is already backed by Treasuries, resulting in little net new buying for the $40 trillion deficit.

## AI Evolution and the Energy Challenge
* **From Generative to Agentic AI:** The industry is moving beyond "prompt and response" (ChatGPT) to "AI Agents" that have autonomous control over computers and file execution.
* **The Energy Paradox:** AI data centers now consume more electricity in some regions (e.g., Wisconsin) than the entire residential population.
    * **Small Modular Reactors (SMRs):** Bianco suggests tech "hyperscalers" should build their own power sources, specifically SMRs, to provide net energy back to the grid. 
    * Success depends on the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) and the environmental lobby allowing modern, non-water-cooled reactors (like TerraPower’s sodium-cooled design) to proliferate.
* **Social Risk:** Similar to the Industrial Revolution, AI risks a "pushback" if job losses in sectors like driving and retail occur before new industries are created to absorb the labor.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "We have got used to that 2010 to 2020 period where no matter what the Fed did... the inflation rate never got above 2%. You can't do that if we've got inflation. If they were to try and be easy in this type of environment, you could wind up with higher interest rates and actually making things worse." — **Jim Bianco**

> "I've yet to meet a real estate guy who has not met an interest rate that he doesn't think should go lower. So I'm not surprised that at every turn [Donald Trump] just keeps demanding lower and lower interest rates." — **Jim Bianco**

> "The Federal Reserve will become the world central bank by default... If you run your financial system poorly or you try to devalue your currency a lot, your population is going to migrate to our currency, the dollar, through a stablecoin." — **Jim Bianco**

> "The concern is the jobs get lost first, the new jobs get created later, and in that gap people get angry... We might get a pushback against this... some kind of collective socialist type of argument to put up a barrier." — **Jim Bianco**

briefings.title: Palantir CEO on Iran, AI Weapons and America's Advantage | a16z American Dynamism Summit
briefings.tldr: America has re-established a decisive technological deterrent against adversaries like China and Russia, but this advantage is fragile; Silicon Valley must embrace its obligation to the warfighter and national defense or risk the eventual nationalization of the technology industry.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
America has re-established a decisive technological deterrent against adversaries like China and Russia, but this advantage is fragile; Silicon Valley must embrace its obligation to the warfighter and national defense or risk the eventual nationalization of the technology industry.

## The Re-establishment of American Deterrence
*   **Technological Dominance:** Karp asserts that America has regained a deterrent capability that was previously "eviscerated." This is driven by a hybrid of software, hardware, and AI—evidenced by recent operations where U.S. technology demonstrated total dominance over adversarial systems.
*   **The Decisive Vote:** In a world of competing powers (U.S., China, Russia), military superiority is the only way for the West to maintain a "decisive vote" on global rules and human rights.
*   **The Warfighter Priority:** Palantir’s core mission is ensuring American warfighters return home safely while ensuring adversaries do not. Karp argues that those who benefit from American freedom yet refuse to support the military are "effing spoiled."
*   **Meritocracy in Defense:** The Department of Defense is highlighted as America's most revered and meritocratic institution, serving as a primary vehicle for social mobility across all demographics.

## The Silicon Valley Wake-Up Call
*   **Risk of Nationalization:** Karp warns that if Silicon Valley continues to automate white-collar jobs while simultaneously distancing itself from the military, a "horseshoe effect" will occur where both political wings agree to nationalize the tech industry.
*   **Strategic Blindness:** He critiques elite tech leaders for having high IQs but low strategic awareness regarding the political consequences of their isolationism.
*   **The "Hollywood" Model:** Karp suggests the tech industry needs a self-regulatory framework similar to the Hollywood rating system to address ethical concerns (privacy, Fourth Amendment rights) before Washington imposes "butchered" regulations.
*   **Bridge Building:** There is a fundamental cultural "language barrier" between Silicon Valley and the Department of Defense. Founders must move beyond elite bubbles—visiting military bases and middle-America—to understand the perspectives of those using their technology.

## The Zero-Sum Reality of AI
*   **Global Competition:** While Silicon Valley prefers to view technology as "positive-sum," Karp argues the AI race is strictly zero-sum. If the U.S. does not set the rules through dominance, China or Russia will.
*   **Palantir’s Competitive Niche:** Karp positions Palantir as the "last company standing" in the AI race because it focuses on the specificity, security, and orchestration (ontology) of data rather than just the underlying Large Language Models (LLMs).
*   **Privacy vs. Utility:** He defines Palantir as an "anti-surveillance" company, arguing that the protection of Fourth Amendment rights is essential even as technology becomes capable of imputing private behavior.

## Cultivating Neurodivergent Talent
*   **The American Advantage:** Karp identifies America’s single greatest competitive advantage as its ability to protect and augment unconventional, "neurodivergent" talent (e.g., individuals with dyslexia or autism).
*   **Individualism as Strategy:** The U.S. wins by allowing iconoclastic individuals to follow their own "playbooks" rather than forcing them into bureaucratic "straight jackets."
*   **Management Philosophy:** Karp views himself as an "artist" who manages high-aptitude outliers by helping them express unique solutions that only they could build, then "anti-dyslexifying" their workflow to ensure those solutions scale within a corporate or military framework.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "We are the power that actually has the decisive vote. And there is only one way to do that, and that is with military superiority." — **Alex Karp**

> "If Silicon Valley believes we are going to take away everyone's white-collar job... and you're going to screw the military... if you don't think that's going to lead to nationalization of our technology, you're retarded." — **Alex Karp**

> "Our single advantage is to augment neurodivergent, highly individual people to be their absolute unique best and protect their First, Second, Fourth, and Fifth Amendment rights so that they don't get screwed." — **Alex Karp**

briefings.title: Scott Galloway: why tackling the 'crisis of masculinity' would also help close the gender gap
briefings.tldr: The "crisis of masculinity" is a systemic issue where young men are falling behind in education, economic viability, and mental health, yet Scott Galloway argues that lifting men up is entirely compatible with—and necessary for—the continued progress of women and Western society.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The "crisis of masculinity" is a systemic issue where young men are falling behind in education, economic viability, and mental health, yet Scott Galloway argues that lifting men up is entirely compatible with—and necessary for—the continued progress of women and Western society.

## The Data: A Rapid Decline for Young Men
*   **Stagnating Social Milestones:** One in three men live at home at age 25, and one in five still live at home at age 30. Only one in three men are currently in a relationship, compared to two in three women.
*   **Educational Gaps:** There is a 60/40 female-to-male ratio in college attendance, with men dropping out at significantly higher rates.
*   **Mental Health Crisis:** Men account for four out of every five suicide deaths.
*   **The Empathy Gap:** Galloway suggests young men receive less empathy because older generations of men held an "unfair advantage" (white, heterosexual males garnered 1/3 of global economic growth between 1945–1995). Current young men are being "held accountable" for the privileges of their predecessors.

## Redefining Masculinity and "The Code"
*   **Aspirational Masculinity:** Galloway argues that "toxic masculinity" is an oxymoron; masculinity should be defined as the instinct to protect, provide, and procreate. 
*   **Valor vs. Aggression:** While male aggression is often pathologized, Galloway cites the **Carnegie Award** for heroism—77 of 81 awards last year went to men—as proof that the same traits can manifest as life-saving valor.
*   **Rejecting the Extremes:** 
    *   The far right recognizes the crisis but offers a "coarse and cruel" return to the 1950s.
    *   The far left often suggests men should simply "act more like women," which Galloway argues is unhelpful.
*   **The Need for a Operating System:** With the decline of religious institutions and the military, young men lack a "code" to guide decision-making.

## Macro-Economic and Policy Reforms
*   **Education Reform:** "Red-shirt" boys by starting them in kindergarten a year later than girls to account for biological developmental gaps (roughly 18 months). Galloway also advocates for expanding freshman class sizes at universities to end "rejectionist culture."
*   **Wealth Redistribution:** Current economic policies (mortgage interest deductions, capital gains tax breaks) transfer wealth from the young and mobile to the old and established. 
*   **Housing and Infrastructure:** Shift from "drill baby drill" to "build baby build" to make homeownership attainable for young people, which is a key driver of romantic and social stability.
*   **National Service:** Implement mandatory national service to foster empathy across different demographics and reduce the isolation and depression seen in the "screen-only" generation.

## Individual Agency: The "Rule of Threes"
Galloway encourages young men to exercise their agency through three specific habits to put themselves in the "top 5%" of their cohort:
*   **Physical Health:** Work out at least three times a week.
*   **Economic Engagement:** Spend at least 30 hours a week working outside the home (e.g., Uber, TaskRabbit, or office work) to build professional skills.
*   **Social Connection:** Engage with strangers three times a month via sports leagues, volunteer groups, or religious organizations.
*   **Platonic Friendships:** Galloway emphasizes that having "girl-friends" (platonic) is the best way to understand what women value and to build the social intelligence required for romantic success.

## Bridging the Economic Gender Gap
*   **Investment Imbalance:** Silja Baller noted that less than 20% of private equity leadership is female, and only 2% of VC funding goes to women. 
*   **The "Alpha" in Femtech:** Galloway argues there is significant "alpha" (untapped profit) in female founders and health technologies because the market is currently underinvested. 
*   **Success Breeds Change:** Real shifts in the VC landscape will occur when "greed glands" are activated by multi-billion dollar exits from female-founded companies.

> "Lifting a young man up and also celebrating and being afterburners for women's progress is entirely compatible. Empathy is not a zero-sum game." — **Scott Galloway**

> "We need to restore the greatest alliance in history... the alliance between men and women. And the genders have done a great job of convincing themselves that it's the other gender's fault." — **Scott Galloway**

> "Nothing great is ever going to happen to you on a screen. You need to be in the company of other mammals." — **Scott Galloway**

briefings.title: The Most Founder Mode CEO Working Today Isn’t the Founder: Opendoor’s Kaz Nejatian
briefings.tldr: Kaz Nejatian discusses his "refounding" of Opendoor, arguing that enduring companies are built on the "first derivatives" of their core business and that true "Founder Mode" requires a radical prioritization of outcomes over processes and a total rejection of life’s defaults.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Kaz Nejatian discusses his "refounding" of Opendoor, arguing that enduring companies are built on the "first derivatives" of their core business and that true "Founder Mode" requires a radical prioritization of outcomes over processes and a total rejection of life’s defaults.

## The Theory of "First Derivative" Businesses
* **Core Insight:** Kaz argues that the most successful companies in history are built on the first derivative of their primary business rather than the core activity itself.
    * **Historical Examples:** Union Pacific made more money from land and homes than the railway; Google search is the core, but ads are the high-value first derivative.
    * **Platform Evolution:** Shopify evolved from a SaaS tool into a merchant services powerhouse (payments, tax, billing) because those derivatives provide the long-term enduring value that society often misunderstands.
* **Truth Over Sunk Costs:** Kaz details Shopify’s decision to divest from logistics.
    * **Adaptive Strategy:** The decision took only three weeks because the "facts on the ground" changed; once third-party options like Walmart and DHL became viable, Shopify didn't need to own concrete to serve its merchants.
    * **The "Main Mission":** Leaders must be willing to abandon "side quests" even if they were major investments if those projects no longer serve the core truth of the business.

## Leadership and "Founder Mode" for Non-Founders
* **Outcomes vs. Processes:** Kaz defines the difference between professional managers and founders by their focus.
    * **Process vs. Truth:** Professional managers often prioritize process and appearance because their power comes from management; founders (and founder-mode CEOs) prioritize truth and outcome delivery.
    * **The "Founder Seat":** A company doesn't necessarily need its original founder, but it must have someone occupying the "founder seat" who exerts "exothermic pressure" on the system.
* **Strong Attract, Strong Repel:** Upon taking over Opendoor, Kaz refreshed almost the entire executive team within two quarters.
    * **The User Manual:** Kaz uses a decade-old "Blueprint" (a user manual for working with him) to help employees opt-in or opt-out immediately.
    * **Trust Battery:** Borrowing from Shopify CEO Tobi Lütke, Kaz starts with high trust (75%) but allows it to deplete rapidly if performance or alignment fails.

## Overriding Life and Career Defaults
* **Deliberate Radicalism:** Kaz believes you cannot "half-ass" a change in direction; you must override defaults with full force.
    * **Personal Defaults:** Kaz identifies as a religious tech CEO who reads the Bible daily and goes to church, a choice he made deliberately to stay grounded and avoid the "rat race" of constant comparison.
    * **Stewardship vs. Status:** He advises optimizing for *doing* things (stewardship) rather than *being* things (status). Those who optimize for service often find happiness as a byproduct, whereas those who optimize for happiness directly often fail.
* **Time Horizons:** He views "quarters" as useless metrics.
    * **The Weekly/Decadal Split:** Effective leaders should focus on "this week" (tactical execution/validation) and "ten years from now" (long-term vision).

## The Mechanics of the Opendoor Turnaround
* **Incentive Alignment:** Kaz rejected a standard executive pay package, choosing a $1 salary and performance-based units (PSUs) that have zero value unless the stock performs.
    * **Against RSUs:** He argues that standard RSUs incentivize professional managers to "manage a slow decline" rather than take the risks necessary for a turnaround.
* **AI-Native Transformation:** To shift Opendoor into an AI company, Kaz made "defaulting to AI" a primary metric in performance reviews.
    * **Practical Application:** In a recent company hackathon, a general contractor with no coding experience used tools like Cursor and OpenAI to automate his entire job, transitioning from a manual worker to a manager of software.

## Personal Integration and Resilience
* **Work-Life Integration:** Kaz rejects the standard notion of work-life balance, instead aligning his entire family (wife and children) around the company’s mission.
    * **The Family Mission:** His children understand Opendoor’s product, and he credits his family for providing the resilience needed to survive the "worst days," such as large-scale layoffs.
* **The "Career" Mindset:** He distinguishes between a "job" (doing something for pay) and a "career" (something you work on for yourself).
    * **Craftsmanship:** He advises young professionals to "work all the hours" to find their breaking points and master their craft, noting that the health and wealth benefits of marriage and family are statistically significant for long-term CEO success.

> "Companies are exoskeletons of their leaders if they're good... The question is not whether the founder is there or not; the question is whether the founder seat is taken or not." — Kaz Nejatian

> "Founder mode means taking responsibility for outcomes, not processes. Professional managers care more about process than truth. They care more about what things look like than what they are." — Kaz Nejatian

> "Watching CNBC does not make you a good professional CEO, it just doesn't. I don't genuinely understand CEOs that have the stock price on a Bloomberg terminal in their office." — Kaz Nejatian
